comparisons.title: Cursor vs Claude Code
comparisons.pick: Pick Cursor if you want an AI-first editor: a desktop app with agents, cloud automations and code review, and a free tier to try it. Pick Claude Code if you live in the terminal and want an agent that works across your repo. It has no free tier of its own and comes with a paid Claude plan (Pro from $17/month billed annually). Many developers use both: Cursor for editing, Claude Code for long agentic tasks.
faq: Is Claude Code free?
No. Claude Code has no free tier of its own: it comes with paid Claude plans (Pro from $17/month billed annually or $20 monthly, Max from $100/month) or API usage.
Does Cursor have a free plan?
Yes. Cursor's free plan includes limited agent and chat requests. Paid plans start at $8/month (Plus), and third-party model usage is billed separately on top of plan prices.
Can I use Claude Code and Cursor together?
Yes. Claude Code runs in a terminal, so you can run it inside Cursor's integrated terminal on the same repo and use Cursor for editing and review.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs GitHub Copilot
comparisons.pick: Pick GitHub Copilot if you want to keep your current editor. It plugs into VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode, plus GitHub.com itself, and Pro is $10/month. Pick Cursor if you're happy to switch editors for an AI-native one, where agents, cloud automations and Bugbot review are part of the app rather than a plugin. Cursor's $8 Plus plan is cheaper on paper but limited to Grok models. To use third-party models you need Premium ($30), and that usage is billed at API prices on top.
faq: Which is cheaper, Cursor or GitHub Copilot?

Cursor Plus is $8/month and Copilot Pro is $10/month, as listed on 16 Oct 2026. Cursor Plus only includes Grok models, and third-party models on Cursor's higher plans are billed at API list price. Copilot plans include GitHub AI Credits, with extra usage bought as credits.
Does GitHub Copilot work in JetBrains IDEs?
Yes. GitHub lists VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, the CLI, GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile. Cursor is its own desktop editor (plus CLI, mobile and cloud agents).
Do both have a free plan?
Yes. Copilot Free has limited chat and agent usage and no code review or cloud agent. Cursor Free has limited agent and chat requests.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Windsurf
comparisons.pick: Important first: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop. Cognition renamed it on 2 Jun 2026, and windsurf.com/pricing now redirects to Devin's pricing. Pick Cursor if you want a polished single-editor experience with plans from $8/month. Pick Windsurf/Devin Desktop if you want one screen to run many agents, both Devin's and third-party ones like Codex and Claude Agent via ACP. Its free plan includes unlimited Tab completions, and Pro is $20/month. On both, heavy use of frontier models ends up billed at API prices, so compare your usage, not the sticker price.
faq: Does Windsurf still exist?
Yes, under a new name. Cognition renamed Windsurf to Devin Desktop on 2 Jun 2026. Your editor, extensions and settings carried over, and windsurf.com/pricing redirects to devin.ai/pricing.
How much does Windsurf (Devin Desktop) cost compared with Cursor?

Devin Desktop: Free, Pro $20/month, Max $200/month, Teams $80/month minimum plus $40 per full seat. Cursor: Free, Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100, Ultra $200, Teams from $30/user. Prices as listed on 16 Oct 2026.
What happens when I hit my usage limit?
On both, paid plans include a usage allowance. Devin Desktop bills extra usage at API list prices. Cursor bills third-party model usage at API list price on Premium and above.

comparisons.title: Claude Code vs GitHub Copilot
comparisons.pick: Pick GitHub Copilot if you want help inside the editor you already use, a real free plan, and agents and code review tied to GitHub pull requests. Pro is $10/month. Pick Claude Code if you want a terminal agent that reads and changes your whole repo in long, multi-step runs. It costs more to start, since it comes with Claude Pro ($17/month annual), but you also get the full Claude app. Copilot suits teams standardising on GitHub. Claude Code suits developers who delegate bigger tasks from the command line.
faq: Is GitHub Copilot cheaper than Claude Code?
Yes, at the entry level. Copilot has a free plan and Pro at $10/month. Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan, from $17/month billed annually ($20 monthly).
Does Claude Code work in VS Code?
Claude Code is a terminal tool, so you can run it in VS Code's integrated terminal. Copilot installs as a native extension in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode.
Which one reviews pull requests?
Copilot includes code review and a cloud agent on paid plans, but not on Free. Claude Code works on your local repo from the terminal.

comparisons.title: Claude Code vs Windsurf
comparisons.pick: Windsurf has been renamed Devin Desktop (June 2026), so this is really Claude Code against Cognition's agent IDE. Pick Claude Code if you want Anthropic's agent in your terminal, bundled with a Claude subscription. Pick Windsurf/Devin Desktop if you want a graphical IDE with a free plan that can also host Claude Agent itself through ACP, next to Devin and Codex, in one Kanban view. Using Claude Agent inside Devin Desktop doesn't make the costs go away: model usage still comes from somewhere.
faq: Can I use Claude inside Windsurf/Devin Desktop?
Yes. Devin Desktop lists Claude Agent among the ACP-compatible agents it supports at launch, and Pro includes frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.
Which has a free plan?
Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) has a Free plan with a light agent quota and unlimited Tab completions. Claude Code has no free tier.
Is Claude Code an IDE?
No. Claude Code is a terminal-based agent. Devin Desktop is a full desktop IDE built on the Windsurf editor.

comparisons.title: Windsurf vs GitHub Copilot
comparisons.pick: Pick GitHub Copilot if you want to stay in VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio or Xcode and keep everything on GitHub. It's $10/month for Pro and runs in more editors than anything else here. Pick Windsurf, now Devin Desktop, if you'll switch to a dedicated agent IDE in exchange for running multiple local and cloud agents (Devin Cloud on Pro, $20/month) from one board. For teams, Copilot's seat model is simpler. Devin Desktop Teams has an $80/month minimum plus $40 per full seat.
faq: Is Windsurf the same as Devin Desktop?
Yes. Cognition renamed Windsurf to Devin Desktop on 2 Jun 2026. The Cascade agent was replaced by Devin Local.
Which is cheaper for a solo developer?
Copilot Pro is $10/month and Devin Desktop Pro is $20/month. Both have free plans.
Do they support my IDE?
Copilot is an extension for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode. Devin Desktop is its own desktop editor rather than a plugin.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Continue.dev
comparisons.pick: This matchup has a twist: Cursor acquired Continue in 2026. Continue's GitHub repo is now read-only and 2.0.0 was its final release. Pick Cursor if you want a maintained product with ongoing updates. Continue's open-source extension still runs with your own model keys or local models, so it's only worth considering if you need a frozen, self-run setup and accept that nothing will be fixed. If you liked Continue's bring-your-own-model approach, Cline is the closest maintained alternative on ToolRank.
faq: Is Continue.dev discontinued?
Yes. continue.dev now says Continue was acquired by Cursor, and the GitHub README says the repository is no longer actively maintained and is read-only, with 2.0.0 as the final release.
Can I still use Continue?
The open-source code remains available, so you can keep running the extension with your own API keys or local models. It just won't get updates.
What should Continue users switch to?
Cursor (which acquired Continue) if you want an AI editor, or a maintained open-source agent like Cline if you want to keep bringing your own models.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Cody (Sourcegraph)
comparisons.pick: For individuals this isn't a real choice any more. Sourcegraph stopped new Cody Free and Pro sign-ups in June 2025 and discontinued those plans, and its successor product Amp spun out as a separate company in December 2025. Pick Cursor if you're an individual or small team. Pick Cody only if your company already runs Sourcegraph Enterprise (from a $16K annual minimum) and wants AI grounded in Sourcegraph's code search across very large codebases.
faq: Is Sourcegraph Cody still available?
Only for enterprises. Cody Free and Pro were discontinued in 2025, and Cody continues as part of Sourcegraph Enterprise.
Was Cody renamed Amp?
Not exactly. Amp is a separate agentic product that Sourcegraph pointed Cody Free/Pro users to. Amp then spun out as an independent company in December 2025.
How much does Sourcegraph Enterprise cost?
Sourcegraph's pricing page lists Enterprise starting at a $16K minimum annual contract, including credits for AI features (checked 16 Oct 2026).

comparisons.title: Claude Code vs Aider
comparisons.pick: Both live in the terminal, so the difference is the business model. Aider is free and open source (Apache-2.0). You plug in any model, including DeepSeek or a local one, and pay only your provider. Every change is a git commit you can undo. Claude Code is Anthropic's own agent, bundled into Claude plans from $17/month, built for longer autonomous runs across a repo. Pick Aider for cost control and model freedom. Pick Claude Code if you already pay for Claude and want the most capable agent from that vendor without wiring up API keys.
faq: Is Aider free?
Yes. Aider is open source, so you only pay for the LLM you connect (or nothing, with a local model).
Can Aider use Claude models?
Yes. Aider's docs show running it with Claude Sonnet via an Anthropic API key, as well as DeepSeek, OpenAI and local models.
Which is more actively developed?
Claude Code is a core Anthropic product. Aider's GitHub repo had its last push on 22 May 2026 (as of 16 Oct 2026), so check recent releases before standardising on it.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Replit Agent
comparisons.pick: These solve different problems. Replit Agent lives in the browser: describe an app and it builds, adds a database and deploys it, with no local setup. Core is $20/month ($18 annual) and includes $20 of model credit. Cursor is a desktop editor for working in your own repo, with agents, code review and plans from $8/month. Founders and non-specialists shipping a hosted app should start with Replit. Developers maintaining real codebases with their own tooling should pick Cursor.
faq: Do I need to install anything for Replit Agent?
No. Replit runs in the browser (and on mobile). Cursor is a desktop app with a CLI.
How much does Replit Agent cost?
Replit lists Core at $20/month ($18 billed annually) and Pro at $100/month ($90 annually), each including that amount toward AI models. We couldn't confirm free-plan limits from its pricing page.
Can Replit host my app?
Yes. Deployments and databases are built in. Cursor edits code and you deploy it however you normally would.

comparisons.title: Claude Code vs Devin
comparisons.pick: Pick Claude Code if you want to stay in the loop: it runs in your terminal on your machine, you watch it work, and you steer it. Pick Devin if you want to hand off tickets entirely. It runs in the cloud, takes tasks from Slack, Linear or Jira, and comes back with PRs on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket. Devin's self-serve plans now start free, but cloud agents need Pro ($20/month). Claude Code starts at $17/month (annual) through Claude Pro.
faq: Does Devin have a free plan?
Yes, as of 16 Oct 2026. Devin's Free plan includes a light quota and limited models. Cloud agents (Devin Cloud) start on Pro at $20/month.
Where does each one run?
Claude Code runs in your local terminal. Devin runs agents in the cloud (and locally through Devin Desktop) and integrates with Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira and git hosts.
Which is better for big refactors?
Claude Code suits interactive, supervised refactors in your repo. Devin suits well-scoped tasks you can delegate and review as a PR. Either way, review the diff.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Bolt.new
comparisons.pick: Pick Bolt.new if you want an app running in your browser in minutes from a prompt, with no install and no repo. Its free plan gives 300K tokens a day (1M a month) and Pro is $25/month. Pick Cursor if you're a developer working on an existing codebase, or you want full control over files, git and deployment. A common path is to prototype in Bolt, then move the code into Cursor once it needs real engineering.
faq: Is Bolt.new free?
Yes. The free plan includes 300K tokens/day and 1M tokens/month, with Bolt branding on sites. Pro starts at $25/month billed monthly.
Do I need coding skills for Cursor?
It helps. Cursor is a code editor built for developers. Bolt.new is aimed at prompting a full-stack app into existence in the browser.
Can I move a Bolt project into Cursor?
Yes. Bolt produces normal web app code, which you can continue editing in any editor, including Cursor.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Lovable
comparisons.pick: Pick Lovable if you're a founder, designer or non-developer who wants to chat an app into existence and host it on Lovable Cloud. The free plan gives 5 build credits a day, capped at 30 a month. Pick Cursor if you write code and want an AI editor and agents working in your own repo. Lovable's paid prices didn't render in the page text we fetched, so check its pricing page directly. Cursor's start at $8/month.
faq: Is Lovable good for developers?
It's built for people who'd rather describe an app than code it. Developers usually prefer an editor like Cursor for control over the code.
What does Lovable's free plan include?
5 build credits a day (up to 30 a month) plus 20 Cloud credits a month, per Lovable's pricing page on 16 Oct 2026.
Does Lovable host my app?
Yes, through Lovable Cloud. Cursor doesn't host apps. It's an editor.

comparisons.title: Windsurf vs Continue.dev
comparisons.pick: Neither product exists under its old name. Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (Cognition, June 2026), and Continue was acquired by Cursor, with its repo read-only after a final 2.0.0 release. If you want something maintained, the real choice is Devin Desktop (free plan, Pro $20/month) or another live tool. Keep running Continue's open-source extension only if you need a self-run, bring-your-own-model setup and can live without updates.
faq: What happened to Windsurf?
Cognition renamed it Devin Desktop on 2 Jun 2026. Plans, settings and extensions carried over.
What happened to Continue.dev?
Continue was acquired by Cursor. Its GitHub repo is no longer maintained and is read-only, and 2.0.0 was the final release.
Is there a maintained open-source alternative?
Yes. Cline is free and open source with bring-your-own-key, and is actively maintained (checked 16 Oct 2026).

comparisons.title: GitHub Copilot vs Continue.dev
comparisons.pick: Continue was long the open-source answer to Copilot, but Continue has been acquired by Cursor and is no longer maintained. Pick GitHub Copilot if you want a supported assistant in VS Code, JetBrains and more, with a free plan and Pro at $10/month. Only stay on Continue's final open-source release if you specifically need local models or full control and accept frozen software. If open source matters to you, compare Copilot with Cline instead.
faq: Is Continue.dev a free Copilot alternative?
It was, but the project is now discontinued and read-only after Cursor acquired it. The code still runs with your own keys or local models, without updates.
Does Copilot have a free plan?
Yes. Copilot Free includes limited chat and agent usage. Pro is $10/month.
Can Copilot use local models?
We haven't verified local-model support for Copilot. Continue's final release supports local models through your own setup.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Zed AI
comparisons.pick: Pick Zed if speed comes first: it's a fast native open-source editor that stays free forever when you bring your own API keys or external agents like Claude Agent and Codex CLI. Pro is $10/month with unlimited edit predictions and $5 of tokens. Pick Cursor if you want the deepest built-in agent features, like cloud agents, automations and Bugbot code review, and don't mind a VS Code-style editor. Zed bills hosted usage at API list price plus 10%. Cursor bills third-party models at API list price on Premium.
faq: Is Zed free?
Yes. Zed's Personal plan is free forever, with unlimited use through your own API keys or external agents. Pro ($10/month) adds Zed-hosted models and unlimited edit predictions.
Can I use Claude in Zed?
Yes. Zed supports external agents including Claude Agent and Codex CLI, and providers like Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock, OpenRouter and Ollama.
Does Zed run VS Code extensions?
No. Zed has its own extension system. Cursor is built on the VS Code ecosystem.

comparisons.title: Claude Code vs Amazon Q Developer
comparisons.pick: Amazon Q Developer is being retired. AWS closed new sign-ups on 15 May 2026, the Q CLI became Kiro CLI, and IDE plugins and paid subscriptions reach end of support on 30 Apr 2027. New users can't choose it. Pick Claude Code for a terminal agent from Anthropic, from $17/month. If you're tied to AWS, compare Claude Code with Kiro, AWS's successor, which also offers Claude models and has a free tier.
faq: Can I still sign up for Amazon Q Developer?
No. AWS blocked new Q Developer accounts and subscriptions from 15 May 2026. Existing customers keep access until 30 Apr 2027.
What replaces Amazon Q Developer?
Kiro. AWS's announcement points users to Kiro (IDE and CLI), and the Q CLI has already become Kiro CLI.
Does Amazon Q use Claude?
Q Developer's pricing page lists access to the latest Claude models. AWS says the newest coding models are now only on Kiro.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Tabnine
comparisons.pick: Pick Cursor if you're an individual or a team wanting a self-serve AI editor today, with a free plan and paid plans from $8/month. Tabnine was acquired by Tricentis in 2026, and tabnine.com now redirects to Tricentis, so we couldn't re-verify its current plans. Its historical strength is private, on-prem and air-gapped deployment for enterprises. If that's your requirement, contact Tricentis directly. Otherwise Cursor is the straightforward choice.
faq: Is Tabnine still available?
Tabnine is now part of Tricentis. tabnine.com redirects to Tricentis with a notice, and links for existing users to log in and find docs. We couldn't verify current self-serve plans.
How much does Tabnine cost?
Not yet verified: the vendor pricing page redirected when we checked on 16 Oct 2026. Ask Tricentis for a quote.
Which is better for air-gapped environments?
Tabnine has historically offered on-prem and air-gapped deployment for enterprises. We haven't verified an air-gapped option for Cursor.

comparisons.title: Claude Code vs Codeium
comparisons.pick: Codeium no longer exists as a brand. It became Windsurf, and Windsurf became Devin Desktop in June 2026. codeium.com now redirects to Devin Desktop. So the real comparison is Claude Code against Devin Desktop. Pick Claude Code for Anthropic's terminal agent with a Claude plan (from $17/month). Pick Devin Desktop if you want a free IDE with unlimited Tab completions and an agent board, with Pro at $20/month.
faq: What happened to Codeium?
Codeium was renamed Windsurf, and Windsurf was renamed Devin Desktop by Cognition on 2 Jun 2026. codeium.com redirects to devin.ai/desktop.
Is Codeium's free autocomplete still available?
Its successor, Devin Desktop, has a Free plan with unlimited Tab completions and a light agent quota.
Does Claude Code do autocomplete?
No. Claude Code is an agent you instruct in the terminal, not an inline autocomplete tool.

comparisons.title: Windsurf vs Cody (Sourcegraph)
comparisons.pick: Both have changed a lot. Windsurf is now Devin Desktop, and Cody is enterprise-only after Sourcegraph discontinued Free and Pro in 2025. For an individual or small team, Devin Desktop is the only one of the two you can sign up for: Free, or Pro at $20/month. Cody makes sense only inside an existing Sourcegraph Enterprise deployment (from $16K/year), where its value is code-search context across huge monorepos.
faq: Can individuals still use Cody?
No. Cody Free and Pro were discontinued in 2025. Cody remains part of Sourcegraph Enterprise.
Is Windsurf still sold?
Yes, as Devin Desktop (renamed 2 Jun 2026): Free, Pro $20/month, Max $200/month and Teams plans.
Which handles very large codebases better?
Sourcegraph's strength is code search across very large codebases. Devin Desktop offers 'Fast Context' and cloud agents. We haven't benchmarked either.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs Roo Code
comparisons.pick: Roo Code shut down on 15 May 2026 and its GitHub repo is archived, so pick Cursor if you want a maintained AI editor. If you used Roo for its open-source, bring-your-own-model agent in VS Code, the Roo team itself points to Cline (the project Roo was forked from) or the community fork ZooCode. Kilo Code is another Roo-lineage option listed on ToolRank.
faq: Is Roo Code discontinued?
Yes. The Roo Code extension was shut down on 15 May 2026 and the RooCodeInc/Roo-Code repository is archived.
What's the best Roo Code alternative?
The Roo team suggests Cline or the community fork ZooCode. If you want a full AI editor rather than an extension, Cursor is the top-ranked option on ToolRank.
Was Roo Code free?
Yes. The extension was free and open source (Apache-2.0), and you paid your own model provider.

comparisons.title: Claude Code vs Cline
comparisons.pick: Pick Cline if you want the agent free and open source, inside VS Code (or the CLI), with any model from Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Bedrock and more. You pay only for inference, at cost or with your own keys. Pick Claude Code if you'd rather pay one Claude subscription (from $17/month) than per-token bills, and you're happy in the terminal. Heavy users often find a subscription more predictable than paying per token. Light users usually spend less with Cline.
faq: Is Cline free?
Yes. The open-source extension is free for individuals, and you pay only for AI inference, either with your own API keys or the Cline provider at cost.
Can Cline use Claude models?
Yes. Cline supports Anthropic along with OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex and others.
Does Claude Code work in VS Code?
Claude Code runs in a terminal, including VS Code's integrated terminal. Cline is a native VS Code extension.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs OpenHands
comparisons.pick: Pick OpenHands if you want an autonomous agent you can run locally for free, self-host, or audit line by line. It's MIT-licensed and model-agnostic, with a free cloud tier capped at 10 conversations a day. Pick Cursor if you want an editor first, where you code alongside agents with completions, review and cloud agents in one polished app. Teams with strict data rules lean towards OpenHands' self-hosting. Individual developers usually get more done day to day in Cursor.
faq: Is OpenHands free?
Yes. The open-source version is free with unlimited local conversations, and OpenHands Cloud Individual is free with 10 conversations a day. You pay your own LLM costs.
Can I self-host OpenHands?
Yes. Open source runs locally, and Enterprise can be self-hosted in your VPC.
Is OpenHands a code editor?
No. It's an agent with a web GUI, terminal UI, CLI and SDK. Cursor is a desktop code editor.

comparisons.title: GitHub Copilot vs Amazon Q Developer
comparisons.pick: New users can only pick one of these: AWS stopped new Amazon Q Developer sign-ups on 15 May 2026, and plugins and paid subscriptions end on 30 Apr 2027. Pick GitHub Copilot for a supported assistant across VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio, Eclipse and Xcode, with a free plan and Pro at $10/month. Existing Q customers with Java or .NET upgrades in flight should finish them before the cutoff and plan a move. AWS's own path is Kiro.
faq: Is Amazon Q Developer being discontinued?
Yes, for the IDE plugins and paid subscriptions: end of support is 30 Apr 2027, and new sign-ups closed on 15 May 2026.
How did pricing compare?
Q Developer Pro was $19/user/month with a free tier of 50 agentic requests a month (existing accounts only now). Copilot Pro is $10/month, and Copilot also has a free plan.
What happens to Java upgrades in Q?
AWS says Java upgrades and .NET porting via the Q Developer IDE plugins need a paid subscription and won't be accessible after 30 Apr 2027.

comparisons.title: Cursor vs JetBrains AI Assistant
comparisons.pick: Pick JetBrains AI if IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm or another JetBrains IDE is home. AI Pro is $10/month on personal pricing, and JetBrains Air now runs Junie alongside Claude Agent, Codex and Copilot, with your own keys if you like. Pick Cursor if you're on VS Code or don't mind switching, and want an editor built around AI from the ground up. The deciding factor is usually your IDE: JetBrains users rarely want to give up its refactoring and inspections.
faq: How much does JetBrains AI cost?
JetBrains' store lists AI Pro at $10/month ($100/year) and AI Ultimate at $30/month ($300/year) on personal pricing, as of 16 Oct 2026. We didn't verify business pricing or free-tier limits.
What is Junie?
Junie is JetBrains' coding agent, now part of JetBrains Air, which can also run Claude Agent, Codex, Copilot and other ACP agents.
Can I use Cursor with JetBrains IDEs?
Cursor is its own editor, not a JetBrains plugin. If you want AI inside JetBrains, use JetBrains AI or another plugin such as GitHub Copilot.
